Settings
Keys and connection
Every key, proxy value and model choice is here in one place. Keys and tokens stay in this browser only.
Yard shown
Demo yard shows Municipal Harbor: a real Chicago lakefront harbor on the live satellite view, with five years of made-up boats, owners and service, for showing the dashboard to anyone. Live yard shows your own yard, with live Transform data when Use live data is on. The choice is kept in this browser. A link can pick one too: add ?yard=demo or ?yard=live to the page address.
Transform
Map on a phone or tablet
Add ?view=map to the page address for the map alone, sized for a phone or tablet, as the Transform app opens it. Each phone or tablet is connected once with a device code from here. The code holds the proxy address and token, so send it only to yourself and delete the message after pasting it.
Reads the boat records from your Transform form and shows them in place of the demo boats. Browsers can't call Transform directly, so the dashboard goes through a proxy. With the Google Apps Script proxy, the Transform key stays in the script and this browser keeps only the proxy token. A Cloudflare proxy needs the key here instead, and has to allow GetFormInstancesArrayForFormId. If the connection is off or fails, the demo boats show.
Gemini
Used for the demo boat photos, the Gemini voice and the AI checks.
Used by AI check and Confirm with AI. Type a model name to use one not in the list. If the model is refused, the next one in the list is tried. Saved in this browser.
Makes the boat photos (Settings, Photos), with the Gemini key above.
Google Maps (satellite imagery)
Satellite opens on Esri World Imagery and switches to Google as soon as Google's pictures arrive; without a key, or if Google doesn't answer, it stays on Esri. The key stays in this browser only. The key's project needs the Map Tiles API turned on.
Map
Areas and rows
Every area has a number that never changes, so boats and their history stay linked when you rename an area or change a yard's rows. Names marked ? are our guesses.
Planned moves
When a job says a boat should move (to a shop, say), a dotted line runs to a dashed outline where it should be. Off: only the selected boat shows it, and every boat does while Unconfirmed moves is on. Saved in this browser.
Sketch on the satellite
Solid fills in the yard ground, every area, every dock and the water along the docks, so boats that were there when the photo was taken don't show; roads, the rail and the far water still do. See-through only tints the areas, so the boats in the photo show through them. Every browser starts on Solid. Satellite only always shows the photo by itself. Saved in this browser.
Satellite fade
30%
Washes the satellite photo toward white so the real boats and cars in it drop back behind the sketch. 0% shows the photo at full strength. Satellite only always shows the full photo. Saved in this browser.
Boat labels
Zoom in close on the sketch or the satellite and each boat shows a label on its hull. Tick any mix of name, ID and owner; with none ticked, no labels show. Saved in this browser.
Boat size
Packed tight stands the boats in each storage building and South Yard row next to each other, the way the yard really is, and draws them as large as the row allows, up to the size picked here. Each boat stays in its row and on its side of the row. Spread out puts every boat back in its own spot on the sketch, at true scale. Boats grow and shrink with the zoom either way. Saved in this browser.
Bow over transom
How many feet a boat's bow may reach over the transom of the boat ahead when boats are packed tight. These numbers are our estimates for the crew to tune, because BoatFile has no bow or transom heights. A boat's own setting in the app (Bow over the boat ahead) wins over these, even with No overlap picked. It applies where boats stand bow to stern in a line, like the storage building lanes. Saved in this browser.
Area labels
The area and building names on the sketch and on the satellite with the sketch. Show on hover keeps them out of the way: point at an area and its name shows in its usual place (on a tablet, tap the area). Show on hover and Hide also take the street, rail and listing notes off the satellite. The Area labels button by the zoom controls switches them too. Saved in this browser.
Filters gliding away
With one boat picked, the filter row and the tiles glide up out of the way; Reset brings them back at the same pace. If this computer is set to reduce motion, they change at once. Saved in this browser.
Line up the layout with the photo
Building and storage positions are estimated. Nudge the whole layout until it sits on the real yard. Your setting is saved in this browser.
Service moves
For each department, and for any service under it: does the boat stay where it is for the work, or move to an area? A service set to Same as department follows its department; a service's own setting wins over its department's. When staff answer stays or moves in the form, that answer always wins. A move the setting expects but nobody recorded shows as a dashed outline and counts in Unconfirmed moves.
Department or serviceDefaultAreaAfter the job
Ask each time: a job with no stays-or-moves answer is flagged in Unconfirmed moves. Saved in this browser.
Voice
Narration voice
Uses the voices built into this browser, free and with no limits. The list shows the voices of the browser you are using, its best ones first: Natural voices in Edge, Google voices in Chrome, Enhanced or Premium voices in Safari. Your pick is saved for this browser. One voice reads every line of a boat's history; a new pick applies from the next Play history.
Gemini reads the Demo tour and the Play history voice-over with the Gemini key in Keys and connection, the first tab in Settings. Each new line is one speech request billed to that key, and a line already made is reused while the page is open. If there is no key or Gemini doesn't answer, the browser voice takes over and a line on the page says so.
Read AI results aloud
Every AI check, history summary and Analysis AI assessment has a Read aloud button. Turn this on to have each one read as soon as it arrives, in the narration voice chosen above and short or detailed like the narration. Press Stop reading, or start Play history, to stop it. Saved in this browser.
AI checks
AI check under a boat's service history sends that boat's work orders, hours, parts and account status, with yard-wide figures for comparison, to Gemini with the key and model in Keys and connection, the first tab in Settings. Owner names and boat names are not sent; customers go as a coded number. Confirm with AI next to Specs sends only the make, model, year, type and our length and beam. Both are read only: nothing is changed in Transform. Each check is one request billed to that key.
What AI check looks for
The first six are always on. The last four can be switched off. Saved in this browser.
Photos
Where the yard keeps boat photos
In the pattern, {N} is the number in the boat ID (2050 for BF-2050), {D1} its first digit, {D2} its first two digits, {ID} the whole boat ID, and {n} the picture letter: a, then b, c and so on, as a.jpg or A.jpg. Crowley's photo server is L:\{D1}\{N}\{n}.jpg, which reads L:\2\2050\a.jpg. Photos taken in Transform always come first; a boat with none in the source keeps its sample photos. Saved in this browser.
Boat photos made by Gemini
Uses the Gemini key and image model in Keys and connection, the first tab in Settings. Each new photo is one image request billed to that key. Photos are saved in this browser, so each one is made only once. Without a key, or with photo making off, each boat shows sample photos matched to its type, size and hull color. All of these are demo pictures, not photos of a real boat.
Logo
Yard logo
Your logo shows at the top of the dashboard, 75 pixels tall, and at the top of the traveler, the internal report and invoices. PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP or SVG all work; a wide logo on a clear or white background looks best. Big pictures are made smaller before they are kept. Each yard keeps its own logo, in this browser only, so the demo yard and your live yard can differ. Reset to default brings back the standard logo for the yard shown.
Sound
Sound effects
Short sounds for clicks, tabs and the map: a chime at each step of Play history, a ratchet when a mechanic works on a boat, a whoosh when a boat moves, and a little fanfare at the end. They are made in the browser, with no sound files. The speaker button in the header switches them on and off too. Saved in this browser.

Areas and rows
Every area has a number that never changes. Boats and their history are linked to the number, so you can rename freely.
Click an area on the map, or type over a name. Untick In use to retire an area; its number stays with its history and is never reused.
Set each yard's rows. New rows get new numbers, existing rows keep theirs, and rows left outside the range are retired unless boats are still in them. You see the changes before anything is applied.
South yard rows 2 to 13 are drawn on the sketch. Rows added here get their numbers right away and are listed as not on our map yet.
Download the list
Download the areas and the row setup as a spreadsheet, edit it in Excel or Google Sheets, and upload it again. Keep each ID as it is. Leave the ID blank on a new line to add an area.
Upload changes
CSV, XLSX or XLS. Nothing is deleted: areas missing from the file stay as they are. You see every change before anything is applied.
Start over
For this demo, names and rows are saved in this browser. In the live system the area list would be kept in Transform, so the form, the dashboard and every user share one list.
